messages:
maya.chen: Morning — overnight backfill for model-refresh (job id backfill-20260316) failed and left a long-running pod. CI alert popped at ~03:10 UTC. Can someone quick-triage?

devon: on it. any logs/exit codes?

deploy-bot: automated: job backfill-20260316 -> failed (exit 137). last restart count: 5. Created 2026-03-16T02:45:11Z.

maya.chen: pasted tail of worker log: 
```
I0316 02:49:03 main.go:112] starting backfill shard=23
W0316 03:09:59 lock.go:78] failed to refresh redis lock: MOVED 12345 10.10.12.34:6379
E0316 03:10:05 backfill.go:201] unrecoverable: s3 upload failed: AccessDenied: Access Denied
exit status 137
```

sasha: MOVED in redis means we hit the cluster redirect; could be transient. but AccessDenied from S3 is concerning — looks like credential rotation might have overlapped with the job window.

priya: if creds rotated, backfill would be blocked and pod retried until oom/killed (137). we should avoid immediate whole-cluster rerun. plan: 1) stop the stuck pod, 2) confirm S3 creds for the service account, 3) clear any redis lock keys for job backfill-20260316, 4) kick a targeted rerun for that job on staging first.

devon: agree. I'll check IAM history and run a quick bisect if needed. @maya.chen can you paste the pipeline link or the commit sha that started that backfill?

maya.chen: pipeline: https://ci.redwood.ai/pipelines/7890 (started by commit c3f5a7d). Last green for this job was c3f0a2b (yesterday).

oncall: if we're going to kill the pod, do it from the active cluster only; don't touch the migration/infra nodes. I can do the kill in 10m so it doesn't conflict with metrics scraping.

devon: I'll start a local bisect between c3f0a2b..c3f5a7d focusing on changes to S3 upload code and service-account rotation scripts. quick command I'll run: `git bisect start --term-old=good --term-new=bad c3f5a7d c3f0a2b` then run the backfill smoke locally using `./scripts/backfill-smoke --shard 23`.

maya.chen: thanks. @oncall feel free to kill the pod now. note: we might need to delete key `backfill:20260316:lock:23` from redis after failover.

deploy-bot: action scheduled: delete pod backfill-20260316-23 on prod in 5m (requested by oncall).

oncall: pod killed. logs preserved at https://logs.redwood.ai/archives/backfill-20260316/23. I removed the redis key and confirmed it's gone.

priya: confirmed IAM rotation event at 02:58 UTC for service-account `backfill-runner`. it looks like rotation completed partially; a subset of nodes still used the old creds for a few minutes. CS says they rolled the key back.

devon: reproduced AccessDenied locally by swapping creds — looks consistent. not a code regression. marking bisect not needed.

maya.chen: OK runway: 1) restore stable creds globally (CS says done), 2) rerun backfill job for shard 23 only, 3) monitor S3 uploads and redis lock metrics for 15m. @devon can you kick the rerun once you confirm your local smoke passes?

devon: smoke passed locally. I'll trigger the rerun now: `./tools/cron-cli rerun --job backfill-20260316 --shards 23 --reason "partial-iam-rotation"`

deploy-bot: rerun scheduled: backfill-20260316-shard-23 (run id rerun-2401234).

maya.chen: awesome — keep an eye on 5xx and s3 errors. post results here and we can close. :thumbsup:

priya: post-rerun check: uploads succeeded, no redis lock errors for 25m. marking job as recovered.

devon: will open a short incident note for cross-team IAM rotation safety checklist and add a pre-rotation canary for long-running cron jobs.

maya.chen: thanks all. closing thread once devon adds the checklist doc. :pray:
